_note: STAGE B · CRITIC. A separate pass over scripts/authoring/authored/csmop.json, judging each question on its own terms: is there exactly one correct answer, are the distractors plausible without being trivially wrong, is it inside the public rule text (data/rules/text/csmop.json), is there a factual red flag, is the Hindi accurate and consistent with data/drafting/structure-terms.json's established CSMOP vocabulary, is the tone right for a serving officer. Every citation was checked against data/rules/text/csmop.json's actual text, including csmop-6-13 (the merged Chapter 5/6 blob) — the urgency-grading passage q019 cites ('The urgency grading advised are Immediate, Priority and Top Priority') is present verbatim in that textId's text.en, so it is grounded despite the odd-looking id. Rejections stay in data/rules/cards/ with reviewState "rejected" and are never served. (Update: csmop-q-013 was corrected — संगम->संघ — and re-approved.)

csmop-q-009.reason: One correct answer, grounded verbatim in Table 7.1's first row ('Ephemeral — No noting is needed'); distractors are the genuine quantum-of-noting descriptions from the table's other rows (repetitive case, problem-solving case), which is exactly the kind of plausible-from-a-neighbouring-provision distractor the checklist wants.

Distractors are plausible but wrong approval/signing chains.

csmop-q-011.reason: One correct answer, grounded verbatim in para 8.4(3) ('written in the third person and bears no salutation or subscription'); distractors describe the genuine conventions of other forms (letter, D.O. letter) misapplied to the O.M., which is the intended trap.

csmop-q-012.reason: One correct answer, grounded verbatim in Table 8.1 rows 2 and 4 (UPSC addressed by letter to its Secretary; Attorney General approached only through the Ministry of Law & Justice); distractors mix real channels used for other authorities in the same table, which is plausible confusion.

csmop-q-013.reason: The front/back/options and citation are all correctly grounded in para 8.9(i)'s 15-plus-15-day rule and would need no change. But the Hindi explanation mistranslates 'a recognized association' as 'मान्यताप्राप्त संगम' — संगम means 'confluence' (as in a meeting of rivers), not 'association'; the correct word is संघ or संगठन. This is a genuine Hindi accuracy defect in reader-facing text, not present in data/drafting/structure-terms.json's vocabulary or anywhere else in this batch, and should not ship as if it were considered administrative Hindi. Fixable by correcting that one word in the explanation.hi field alone; nothing else about the card needs to change. Fixed: संगम (confluence) corrected to संघ (association) in explanation.hi; re-approved.
